## Swipe Card Stack (`swipe-stack`)

Tinder-style deck: drag the top card away and the pile moves up.

- API: `SwipeCardStack(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/SwipeCardStack.swift

### Usage

```swift
SwipeCardStack(profiles) { profile, direction in
    direction == .right ? like(profile) : pass(profile)
} card: { profile in
    ProfileCard(profile)
        .frame(width: 300, height: 420)
}
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI SwipeCardStack (iOS 17+) over a collection of Identifiable items with a card view builder and an onSwipe(item, direction) callback. Show the top 3 cards from the current position (looping by default). Cards behind are scaled down 5% per level and moved down 12 pt per level. The top card follows a DragGesture: offset by the translation, rotate by translation.width / 20 degrees around the bottom anchor, and overlay a green (right) or red (left) wash, masked by the card, whose opacity grows to 25% at the threshold. On release, if the predicted end translation passes 110 pt, fly the card 600 pt off in that direction with easeIn(0.25), then reset the drag without animation, advance the position with a spring so the pile moves up, and call onSwipe. Otherwise spring back. Add Swipe left and Swipe right accessibility actions.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Which way a card left the stack.
public enum SwipeDirection: Sendable {
    case left
    case right
}

/// A Tinder-style deck. The top card follows the finger and tilts; past a
/// threshold it flies off and the cards behind move up. Drag less and it
/// springs back.
public struct SwipeCardStack<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Card: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let visibleCount: Int
    private let loops: Bool
    private let onSwipe: (Data.Element, SwipeDirection) -> Void
    private let card: (Data.Element) -> Card

    @State private var position = 0
    @State private var drag: CGSize = .zero
    @State private var flyingOff: SwipeDirection?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let threshold: CGFloat = 110

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The cards, top card first.
    ///   - visibleCount: How many cards are drawn in the pile.
    ///   - loops: Starts over from the first card when the deck runs out.
    ///   - onSwipe: Called after a card leaves, with the direction it went.
    ///   - card: Builds the view for one item.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        visibleCount: Int = 3,
        loops: Bool = true,
        onSwipe: @escaping (Data.Element, SwipeDirection) -> Void = { _, _ in },
        @ViewBuilder card: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Card
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.visibleCount = visibleCount
        self.loops = loops
        self.onSwipe = onSwipe
        self.card = card
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let elements = Array(items)
        ZStack {
            ForEach(Array(visibleCards(elements).enumerated()).reversed(), id: \.element.id) { depth, item in
                card(item)
                    .modifier(StackedCard(depth: depth, drag: depth == 0 ? drag : .zero, threshold: threshold))
                    .allowsHitTesting(depth == 0)
                    .gesture(depth == 0 ? dragGesture(for: item) : nil)
                    .accessibilityHidden(depth != 0)
                    .accessibilityActions {
                        Button("Swipe left") { swipe(item, .left) }
                        Button("Swipe right") { swipe(item, .right) }
                    }
            }
        }
    }

    private func visibleCards(_ elements: [Data.Element]) -> [Data.Element] {
        guard !elements.isEmpty else { return [] }
        let remaining = loops ? elements.count : max(0, elements.count - position)
        return (0..<min(visibleCount, remaining)).map { elements[(position + $0) % elements.count] }
    }

    private func dragGesture(for item: Data.Element) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture()
            .onChanged { value in
                guard flyingOff == nil else { return }
                drag = value.translation
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                guard flyingOff == nil else { return }
                // Use the predicted end so a quick flick counts too.
                let x = value.predictedEndTranslation.width
                if abs(x) > threshold {
                    swipe(item, x > 0 ? .right : .left)
                } else {
                    withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.6)) { drag = .zero }
                }
            }
    }

    private func swipe(_ item: Data.Element, _ direction: SwipeDirection) {
        flyingOff = direction
        let distance: CGFloat = direction == .right ? 600 : -600
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.2) : .easeIn(duration: 0.25)) {
            drag = CGSize(width: distance, height: drag.height + 40)
        }
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.25) {
            var transaction = Transaction()
            transaction.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(transaction) { drag = .zero }
            withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.8)) { position += 1 }
            flyingOff = nil
            onSwipe(item, direction)
        }
    }
}

/// Places a card in the pile: deeper cards are smaller and lower; the top
/// card follows the drag and tilts away from it.
private struct StackedCard: ViewModifier {
    var depth: Int
    var drag: CGSize
    var threshold: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                // Green or red wash that grows as the card nears the threshold.
                let progress = min(1, abs(drag.width) / threshold)
                (drag.width > 0 ? Color.green : Color.red)
                    .opacity(depth == 0 ? Double(progress) * 0.25 : 0)
                    .mask { content }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .scaleEffect(1 - CGFloat(depth) * 0.05)
            .offset(y: CGFloat(depth) * 12)
            .offset(drag)
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(drag.width / 20)), anchor: .bottom)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Item: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let items = [Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo].enumerated().map { Item(id: $0, color: $1) }
    return SwipeCardStack(items) { item in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
            .fill(item.color.gradient)
            .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
            .overlay(Text("Card \(item.id + 1)").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .padding(40)
}
```

## Parallax Carousel (`parallax-carousel`)

Paging cards whose images slide slower than the cards, for depth.

- API: `ParallaxCarousel(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ParallaxCarousel.swift

### Usage

```swift
ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
    Image(place.photo)
        .resizable()
        .scaledToFill()
}
.frame(height: 240)
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI ParallaxCarousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding. Use a horizontal ScrollView with a LazyHStack (14 pt spacing), .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center), and horizontal contentMargins so each card (78% of the width) snaps to the centre with neighbours peeking. Draw each card's content wider than the card by the parallax factor (0.35), then use .visualEffect to read the card's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space and offset the content by −(distance of the card centre from the viewport centre) × parallax. Finally frame it to the card size and clip it with a continuous rounded rectangle (22 pt), so the image appears to move slower than its frame. With Reduce Motion on, set parallax to 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A paging carousel whose card contents slide slower than the cards
/// themselves, so images seem to sit deeper than the frame around them.
/// Neighbouring cards peek in from both sides.
public struct ParallaxCarousel<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>?
    private let cardWidth: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let parallax: CGFloat
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var internalSelection: Data.Element.ID?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: One card per item.
    ///   - selection: Optional binding to the centred card; set it to scroll.
    ///   - cardWidth: Card width as a fraction of the carousel's width.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cards.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of each card.
    ///   - parallax: How much slower the content moves than its card (0…1).
    ///   - content: The card's content, usually an image. It is drawn wider
    ///     than the card so the parallax never reveals an edge.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>? = nil,
        cardWidth: CGFloat = 0.78,
        spacing: CGFloat = 14,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 22,
        parallax: CGFloat = 0.35,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.selection = selection
        self.cardWidth = cardWidth
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.parallax = parallax
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let width = geometry.size.width * cardWidth
            let strength = reduceMotion ? 0 : parallax
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        content(item)
                            // Extra width on both sides for the content to slide into.
                            .frame(width: width * (1 + strength), height: geometry.size.height)
                            .visualEffect { view, proxy in
                                // How far this card's centre is from the carousel's centre.
                                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))
                                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))?.width ?? frame.width
                                let distance = frame.midX - viewport / 2
                                return view.offset(x: -distance * strength)
                            }
                            .frame(width: width, height: geometry.size.height)
                            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                            .id(item.id)
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
            }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, (geometry.size.width - width) / 2, for: .scrollContent)
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .scrollPosition(id: selection ?? $internalSelection, anchor: .center)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Place: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let colors: [Color]
    }
    let places = [
        Place(id: 0, colors: [.orange, .pink]),
        Place(id: 1, colors: [.teal, .blue]),
        Place(id: 2, colors: [.purple, .indigo]),
        Place(id: 3, colors: [.mint, .green]),
    ]
    return ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
        LinearGradient(colors: place.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
            .overlay(Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill").font(.system(size: 60)).foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8)))
    }
    .frame(height: 220)
}
```

## Expandable Card (`expandable-card`)

Tap the header and the card springs open, un-blurring its detail.

- API: `ExpandableCard(isExpanded:) { } detail: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ExpandableCard.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var isOpen = false

ExpandableCard(isExpanded: $isOpen) {
    Text("Shipping").font(.headline)
} detail: {
    Text("Arrives Thursday. Free returns within 30 days.")
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ExpandableCard<Header, Detail> (iOS 17+) bound to isExpanded. A VStack holds a plain-style Button containing the header, a spacer and a chevron.down that rotates −180° when open, then, if expanded, the detail view. Toggle inside withAnimation(.spring(response 0.45, damping 0.8)) so the card's height springs. Insert the detail with a combined transition of opacity, an 8 pt upward offset and a custom blur transition (radius 6 → 0). The background is a continuous rounded rectangle (16 pt) filled with the background style whose shadow deepens when open. Expose Expanded/Collapsed as the accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease and an opacity transition only.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A card with a tappable header that expands to reveal its detail. The
/// height springs open, the chevron turns, and the detail un-blurs into place.
/// Stack several for an accordion.
public struct ExpandableCard<Header: View, Detail: View>: View {
    @Binding private var isExpanded: Bool
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let header: Header
    private let detail: Detail

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isExpanded: Whether the detail is showing.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of the card.
    ///   - header: Always visible; tapping it toggles the card.
    ///   - detail: Shown below the header when expanded.
    public init(
        isExpanded: Binding<Bool>,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16,
        @ViewBuilder header: () -> Header,
        @ViewBuilder detail: () -> Detail
    ) {
        _isExpanded = isExpanded
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.header = header()
        self.detail = detail()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
            Button {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
                    isExpanded.toggle()
                }
            } label: {
                HStack {
                    header
                    Spacer(minLength: 8)
                    Image(systemName: "chevron.down")
                        .font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(isExpanded ? -180 : 0))
                }
                .padding()
                .contentShape(Rectangle())
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .accessibilityValue(isExpanded ? Text("Expanded") : Text("Collapsed"))

            if isExpanded {
                detail
                    .padding([.horizontal, .bottom])
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    .transition(
                        reduceMotion
                            ? .opacity
                            : .opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: -8)).combined(with: BlurTransition.blur)
                    )
            }
        }
        .background(
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
                .fill(.background)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isExpanded ? 0.12 : 0.06), radius: isExpanded ? 12 : 4, y: isExpanded ? 6 : 2)
        )
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
    }
}

/// Blurs a view while it is inserted or removed.
private struct BlurTransition: ViewModifier {
    var radius: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.blur(radius: radius)
    }

    static var blur: AnyTransition {
        .modifier(active: BlurTransition(radius: 6), identity: BlurTransition(radius: 0))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var open = [true, false, false]

        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(0..<3) { index in
                    ExpandableCard(isExpanded: $open[index]) {
                        Text("Question \(index + 1)").font(.headline)
                    } detail: {
                        Text("Answers expand smoothly with a spring, and the detail fades and un-blurs into place.")
                            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding()
            .background(Color.gray.opacity(0.1))
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Pulse Rings (`pulse-rings`)

Concentric rings expand and fade continuously, like a radar or live dot.

- API: `PulseRings()`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/PulseRings.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    PulseRings(color: .green, count: 3)
        .frame(width: 120, height: 120)
    Circle().fill(.green).frame(width: 24, height: 24)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI PulseRings view (iOS 17+). Draw N stroked circles (default 3, 2 pt line) that each grow from 20% to 100% of the frame while fading from opacity 1 to 0 over a 2 s cycle, evenly phase-offset so a new ring is always emerging. Drive it with TimelineView(.animation) and compute each ring's progress from the timeline date (no @State or repeatForever), so it never drifts and stops when off screen. Hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Concentric rings that continuously expand and fade, like a radar or a
/// "live" indicator. Place it behind an icon or avatar.
///
/// ```swift
/// ZStack {
///     PulseRings(color: .green)
///         .frame(width: 120, height: 120)
///     Circle().fill(.green).frame(width: 24, height: 24)
/// }
/// ```
public struct PulseRings: View {
    private let color: Color
    private let count: Int
    private let duration: Double
    private let lineWidth: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    public init(color: Color = .accentColor, count: Int = 3, duration: Double = 2, lineWidth: CGFloat = 2) {
        self.color = color
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.duration = duration
        self.lineWidth = lineWidth
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: frozen rings at evenly spaced sizes.
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? duration * 0.5 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            ZStack {
                ForEach(0..<count, id: \.self) { index in
                    ring(progress: progress(time: time, index: index))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func progress(time: TimeInterval, index: Int) -> Double {
        let offset = Double(index) / Double(count)
        return (time / duration + offset).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
    }

    private func ring(progress: Double) -> some View {
        Circle()
            .stroke(color, lineWidth: lineWidth)
            .scaleEffect(0.2 + progress * 0.8)
            .opacity(1 - progress)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ZStack {
        PulseRings(color: .green)
            .frame(width: 160, height: 160)
        Circle()
            .fill(.green)
            .frame(width: 28, height: 28)
    }
}
```

## Like Burst (`burst`)

Particles fly outward from the centre when a value changes.

- API: `.burst(trigger:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Burst.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
    .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
    .burst(trigger: isLiked, color: .pink, isEnabled: isLiked)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .burst(trigger:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for "like" feedback. Every time the Equatable trigger changes (and isEnabled is true), spawn a burst in an overlay: 12 small circles (alternating 7 pt and 4 pt) placed evenly around a circle, which move outward from the centre to a ~36 pt radius while shrinking to 30% and fading out with easeOut over 0.6 s. Remove each burst after it finishes, allow overlapping bursts, and never intercept touches. Color, count and radius are parameters.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Small dots that fly outward from the centre of the view, e.g. on a "like"
/// tap. Plays every time `trigger` changes.
struct BurstModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var color: Color
    var count: Int
    var radius: CGFloat
    var isEnabled: Bool

    @State private var bursts: [UUID] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(bursts, id: \.self) { _ in
                        BurstParticles(color: color, count: count, radius: radius)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) {
                // Reduce Motion: skip the particles.
                guard isEnabled, !reduceMotion else { return }
                let id = UUID()
                bursts.append(id)
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.8) {
                    bursts.removeAll { $0 == id }
                }
            }
    }
}

private struct BurstParticles: View {
    let color: Color
    let count: Int
    let radius: CGFloat

    @State private var exploded = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(0..<max(1, count), id: \.self) { index in
                particle(angle: Double(index) / Double(max(1, count)) * 2 * .pi, index: index)
            }
        }
        .onAppear {
            withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.6)) {
                exploded = true
            }
        }
    }

    private func particle(angle: Double, index: Int) -> some View {
        // Alternate particle size and distance so the burst feels organic.
        let size: CGFloat = index.isMultiple(of: 2) ? 7 : 4
        let distance = radius * (index.isMultiple(of: 3) ? 0.75 : 1)
        return Circle()
            .fill(color)
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
            // Scale before offsetting, otherwise the scale also shrinks the
            // travel distance and the particles never leave the icon.
            .scaleEffect(exploded ? 0.3 : 1)
            .offset(
                x: exploded ? CGFloat(cos(angle)) * distance : 0,
                y: exploded ? CGFloat(sin(angle)) * distance : 0
            )
            .opacity(exploded ? 0 : 1)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Emits a burst of particles every time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
    ///     .burst(trigger: isLiked, color: .pink, isEnabled: isLiked)
    /// ```
    func burst<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        color: Color = .pink,
        count: Int = 12,
        radius: CGFloat = 36,
        isEnabled: Bool = true
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(BurstModifier(trigger: trigger, color: color, count: count, radius: radius, isEnabled: isEnabled))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var liked = false
        var body: some View {
            Button {
                liked.toggle()
            } label: {
                Image(systemName: liked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                    .font(.system(size: 44))
                    .foregroundStyle(liked ? Color.pink : Color.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .burst(trigger: liked, isEnabled: liked)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Checkmark Draw (`checkmark`)

A success mark draws itself: circle stroke, fill, then a popping check.

- API: `AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/AnimatedCheckmark.swift

### Usage

```swift
AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: isDone)
    .frame(width: 80, height: 80)

AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: saved, color: .blue, lineWidth: 3)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AnimatedCheckmark view (iOS 17+) with isChecked, color (green) and lineWidth (4 at 60 pt, scaled with size). It is square. Layer three parts in a ZStack: a circle stroke trimmed from 0 to 1 and rotated −90° so it draws clockwise from the top (easeInOut 0.45 s); a filled circle that scales from 0.6 and fades in with a spring after 0.35 s; and a white checkmark path (short stroke down-right, long stroke up-right, round caps and joins) trimmed from 0 to 1 with easeOut 0.3 s after 0.55 s. Finish with a small bouncy scale pop at 0.75 s. Unchecking reverses everything without delays. With Reduce Motion on, replace the sequence with a 0.2 s fade.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A success mark that draws itself: the circle strokes around, fills, then
/// the checkmark is drawn on top with a small pop. Unchecking erases it.
public struct AnimatedCheckmark: View {
    private let isChecked: Bool
    private let color: Color
    private let lineWidth: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isChecked: Draws the mark when true, erases it when false.
    ///   - color: Circle colour; the checkmark is white on top of it.
    ///   - lineWidth: Stroke width, scaled with the view's size (at 60 pt).
    public init(isChecked: Bool, color: Color = .green, lineWidth: CGFloat = 4) {
        self.isChecked = isChecked
        self.color = color
        self.lineWidth = lineWidth
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let side = min(geometry.size.width, geometry.size.height)
            let scale = side / 60
            ZStack {
                Circle()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: isChecked ? 1 : 0)
                    .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth * scale, lineCap: .round))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))
                    .animation(timing(.easeInOut(duration: 0.45)), value: isChecked)
                Circle()
                    .fill(color)
                    .scaleEffect(isChecked ? 1 : 0.6)
                    .opacity(isChecked ? 1 : 0)
                    .animation(timing(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.6).delay(isChecked ? 0.35 : 0)), value: isChecked)
                CheckmarkShape()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: isChecked ? 1 : 0)
                    .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth * 1.2 * scale, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                    .frame(width: side * 0.42, height: side * 0.32)
                    .offset(y: side * 0.02)
                    .animation(timing(.easeOut(duration: 0.3).delay(isChecked ? 0.55 : 0)), value: isChecked)
            }
            .frame(width: side, height: side)
            .scaleEffect(isChecked && !reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.95)
            .animation(timing(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.4).delay(isChecked ? 0.75 : 0)), value: isChecked)
            .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(isChecked ? Text("Done") : Text("Not done"))
    }

    /// Reduce Motion: skip the drawing and just fade.
    private func timing(_ animation: Animation) -> Animation {
        reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : animation
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var checked = false

        var body: some View {
            AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: checked)
                .frame(width: 80, height: 80)
                .onTapGesture { checked.toggle() }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Confetti (`confetti`)

Confetti bursts out of the view, tumbles under gravity and fades.

- API: `.confetti(trigger:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Confetti.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var orders = 0

Button("Complete order") { orders += 1 }
    .confetti(trigger: orders)

Text("🎉 Level up!")
    .confetti(trigger: level, colors: [.yellow, .orange], count: 120)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .confetti(trigger:colors:count:spread:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Each change of the equatable trigger appends a burst with a start date and 80 random pieces, removed after 2.4 s. Each piece has a velocity fanned ±60° around straight up (speed up to 3.2 × spread), a spin rate, a wobble phase, a 5–9 × 8–14 pt size, a colour index and every fourth one is a circle. Draw all bursts in one Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), in an overlay enlarged by .padding(−spread) (160 pt) so confetti flies beyond the view, with hit testing off. Position = origin + velocity × (1 − e^(−1.6t)) / 1.6 + ½ × gravity × t² (air drag plus gravity), rotate by spin × t, scale x by cos(wobble + 8t) to fake turning over, and fade out over the last 0.6 s. With Reduce Motion on, skip the burst.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Confetti that bursts up and out of the view whenever `trigger` changes,
/// then tumbles down under gravity and fades. Drawn in a single `Canvas`, so
/// a few hundred pieces stay cheap.
struct ConfettiModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var colors: [Color]
    var count: Int
    var spread: CGFloat

    @State private var bursts: [ConfettiBurst] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if !bursts.isEmpty {
                    TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                        Canvas { context, size in
                            let now = timeline.date
                            for burst in bursts {
                                burst.draw(in: &context, size: size, time: now.timeIntervalSince(burst.start), colors: colors)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    // Draw well beyond the view's own bounds.
                    .padding(-spread)
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) {
                guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                let burst = ConfettiBurst(count: count, spread: spread)
                bursts.append(burst)
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + ConfettiBurst.lifetime) {
                    bursts.removeAll { $0.id == burst.id }
                }
            }
    }
}

struct ConfettiBurst: Identifiable {
    static let lifetime: Double = 2.4

    struct Piece {
        var velocity: CGVector
        var spin: Double
        var wobble: Double
        var size: CGSize
        var colorIndex: Int
        var isCircle: Bool
    }

    let id = UUID()
    let start = Date()
    let pieces: [Piece]

    init(count: Int, spread: CGFloat) {
        pieces = (0..<max(1, count)).map { index in
            // Mostly upward, fanned out ±60° from vertical.
            let angle = -Double.pi / 2 + Double.random(in: -1.05...1.05)
            let speed = Double.random(in: 0.55...1.0) * Double(spread) * 3.2
            return Piece(
                velocity: CGVector(dx: cos(angle) * speed, dy: sin(angle) * speed),
                spin: Double.random(in: -9...9),
                wobble: Double.random(in: 0...(2 * .pi)),
                size: CGSize(width: .random(in: 5...9), height: .random(in: 8...14)),
                colorIndex: index,
                isCircle: index.isMultiple(of: 4)
            )
        }
    }

    func draw(in context: inout GraphicsContext, size: CGSize, time: Double, colors: [Color]) {
        guard time >= 0, time < Self.lifetime, !colors.isEmpty else { return }
        let origin = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
        let gravity = 900.0
        let drag = 1.6
        // Velocity decays with air drag; position integrates it.
        let decay = (1 - exp(-drag * time)) / drag
        let fade = time > Self.lifetime - 0.6 ? (Self.lifetime - time) / 0.6 : 1
        for piece in pieces {
            let x = origin.x + piece.velocity.dx * decay
            let y = origin.y + piece.velocity.dy * decay + 0.5 * gravity * time * time * 0.55
            var copy = context
            copy.opacity = fade
            copy.translateBy(x: x, y: y)
            copy.rotate(by: .radians(piece.spin * time))
            // Squash horizontally to fake the piece turning over in 3D.
            copy.scaleBy(x: CGFloat(cos(piece.wobble + time * 8)), y: 1)
            let rect = CGRect(
                x: -piece.size.width / 2,
                y: -piece.size.height / 2,
                width: piece.size.width,
                height: piece.isCircle ? piece.size.width : piece.size.height
            )
            let shape = piece.isCircle ? Path(ellipseIn: rect) : Path(rect)
            copy.fill(shape, with: .color(colors[piece.colorIndex % colors.count]))
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Fires a confetti burst from the view each time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Complete order") { orders += 1 }
    ///     .confetti(trigger: orders)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - trigger: Any equatable value; each change fires one burst.
    ///   - colors: Colours the pieces cycle through.
    ///   - count: Pieces per burst.
    ///   - spread: How far beyond the view's bounds confetti may travel.
    func confetti<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .green, .blue, .purple],
        count: Int = 80,
        spread: CGFloat = 160
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ConfettiModifier(trigger: trigger, colors: colors, count: count, spread: spread))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var count = 0

        var body: some View {
            Button("Celebrate 🎉") { count += 1 }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .confetti(trigger: count)
                .frame(width: 400, height: 400)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Loaders (`loaders`)

Five looping activity indicators: spinner, dots, bars, orbit and pulse.

- API: `MotionLoader(.spinner)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/MotionLoader.swift

### Usage

```swift
MotionLoader(.spinner)
    .frame(width: 32, height: 32)

MotionLoader(.dots, color: .secondary)
    .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MotionLoader view (iOS 17+) with a style enum (spinner, dots, bars, orbit, pulse), a color and a speed multiplier. It is square and drives everything from TimelineView(.animation) time, sizing parts relative to its side. Spinner: a round-capped arc whose trim length breathes between 15% and 75% while it rotates. Dots: three dots hopping up in sequence (max(0, sin(6t − i·0.9))) and brightening at the top. Bars: five capsules whose heights follow a sine wave offset per bar. Orbit: two dots circling each other, scaled and layered by a fake depth. Pulse: two rings expanding and fading in turn around a centre dot. Label it "Loading" for accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, show a dot that slowly breathes in opacity.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A set of looping activity indicators. Pick a style; size it with `.frame`.
public struct MotionLoader: View {
    /// The look of the loader.
    public enum Style: String, CaseIterable, Sendable {
        /// An arc that spins while its length breathes.
        case spinner
        /// Three dots hopping in sequence.
        case dots
        /// Equaliser bars rising and falling in a wave.
        case bars
        /// Two dots orbiting each other.
        case orbit
        /// A ring that pulses outward.
        case pulse
    }

    private let style: Style
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - style: Which loader to draw.
    ///   - color: Fill or stroke colour.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the default tempo.
    public init(_ style: Style = .spinner, color: Color = .accentColor, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.style = style
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
            // Reduce Motion: a slow opacity breathe instead of movement.
            let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let side = min(geometry.size.width, geometry.size.height)
                Group {
                    if reduceMotion {
                        Circle()
                            .fill(color)
                            .frame(width: side * 0.4, height: side * 0.4)
                            .opacity(0.4 + 0.4 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 2)))
                    } else {
                        loader(time: time, side: side)
                    }
                }
                .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently)
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func loader(time: Double, side: CGFloat) -> some View {
        switch style {
        case .spinner:
            let breathe = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 3)
            Circle()
                .trim(from: 0, to: 0.15 + 0.6 * breathe)
                .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: side * 0.1, lineCap: .round))
                .rotationEffect(.radians(time * 5))
                .padding(side * 0.05)

        case .dots:
            HStack(spacing: side * 0.1) {
                ForEach(0..<3, id: \.self) { index in
                    let hop = max(0, sin(time * 6 - Double(index) * 0.9))
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: side * 0.22, height: side * 0.22)
                        .offset(y: -side * 0.25 * hop)
                        .opacity(0.5 + 0.5 * hop)
                }
            }
            .offset(y: side * 0.1)

        case .bars:
            HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: side * 0.07) {
                ForEach(0..<5, id: \.self) { index in
                    let level = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 5 - Double(index) * 0.7)
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: side * 0.12, height: side * (0.25 + 0.65 * level))
                }
            }

        case .orbit:
            ZStack {
                ForEach(0..<2, id: \.self) { index in
                    let angle = time * 4 + Double(index) * .pi
                    let depth = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(angle)
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: side * 0.3, height: side * 0.3)
                        .scaleEffect(0.7 + 0.3 * depth)
                        .opacity(0.6 + 0.4 * depth)
                        .offset(x: cos(angle) * side * 0.3)
                        .zIndex(depth)
                }
            }

        case .pulse:
            ZStack {
                ForEach(0..<2, id: \.self) { index in
                    let phase = (time * 0.8 + Double(index) * 0.5).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
                    Circle()
                        .stroke(color, lineWidth: side * 0.06)
                        .scaleEffect(0.2 + 0.8 * phase)
                        .opacity(1 - phase)
                }
                Circle()
                    .fill(color)
                    .frame(width: side * 0.2, height: side * 0.2)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 24) {
        ForEach(MotionLoader.Style.allCases, id: \.self) { style in
            MotionLoader(style)
                .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
        }
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Morphing Blob (`morphing-blob`)

An organic, lava-lamp blob whose outline never stops changing.

- API: `MorphingBlob()`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/MorphingBlob.swift

### Usage

```swift
MorphingBlob(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange])
    .frame(width: 200, height: 200)

MorphingBlob(fill: Color.blue.opacity(0.3), points: 8, wobble: 0.1)
    .overlay(Image(systemName: "mic.fill"))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MorphingBlob view (iOS 17+) generic over a ShapeStyle fill, with a convenience initializer taking colours for a diagonal LinearGradient. Draw a custom Shape in TimelineView(.animation): place N control points (6) evenly around the centre, each at radius base × (1 + wobble × (0.6·sin(1.1t + 1.7i) + 0.4·sin(0.7t + 2.9i))), where base = half the side × (1 − wobble) and wobble is 0.18. Connect them into a smooth closed curve with a Catmull-Rom spline converted to cubic Béziers (control points p1 + (p2 − p0)/6 and p2 − (p3 − p1)/6). Keep a 1:1 aspect ratio and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, freeze the shape.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// An organic blob whose outline keeps morphing, like a lava lamp. Use it as
/// an avatar backdrop, a "listening" indicator or a hero decoration.
public struct MorphingBlob<Fill: ShapeStyle>: View {
    private let fill: Fill
    private let points: Int
    private let wobble: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - fill: Any shape style: a colour, gradient or material.
    ///   - points: Number of lobes around the outline (4…10 looks organic).
    ///   - wobble: How far the outline moves in and out, as a fraction of the radius.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the morphing tempo.
    public init(fill: Fill, points: Int = 6, wobble: CGFloat = 0.18, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.fill = fill
        self.points = points
        self.wobble = wobble
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            BlobShape(
                time: reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed,
                points: points,
                wobble: wobble
            )
            .fill(fill)
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

public extension MorphingBlob where Fill == LinearGradient {
    /// A blob filled with a diagonal gradient.
    init(colors: [Color] = [.purple, .pink, .orange], points: Int = 6, wobble: CGFloat = 0.18, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.init(
            fill: LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing),
            points: points,
            wobble: wobble,
            speed: speed
        )
    }
}

/// A closed, smooth outline through `points` control points whose distance
/// from the centre is a sum of slow sine waves.
struct BlobShape: Shape {
    var time: Double
    var points: Int
    var wobble: CGFloat

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let count = max(3, points)
        let centre = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let baseRadius = min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2 * (1 - wobble)
        let vertices: [CGPoint] = (0..<count).map { index in
            let angle = Double(index) / Double(count) * 2 * .pi
            let i = Double(index)
            // Two waves with unrelated frequencies so the motion never visibly repeats.
            let offset = sin(time * 1.1 + i * 1.7) * 0.6 + sin(time * 0.7 + i * 2.9) * 0.4
            let radius = baseRadius * (1 + wobble * CGFloat(offset))
            return CGPoint(x: centre.x + CGFloat(cos(angle)) * radius, y: centre.y + CGFloat(sin(angle)) * radius)
        }
        return smoothClosedPath(through: vertices)
    }

    /// Catmull-Rom spline through the points, as cubic Béziers.
    private func smoothClosedPath(through p: [CGPoint]) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        let n = p.count
        path.move(to: p[0])
        for i in 0..<n {
            let p0 = p[(i - 1 + n) % n], p1 = p[i], p2 = p[(i + 1) % n], p3 = p[(i + 2) % n]
            let c1 = CGPoint(x: p1.x + (p2.x - p0.x) / 6, y: p1.y + (p2.y - p0.y) / 6)
            let c2 = CGPoint(x: p2.x - (p3.x - p1.x) / 6, y: p2.y - (p3.y - p1.y) / 6)
            path.addCurve(to: p2, control1: c1, control2: c2)
        }
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    MorphingBlob()
        .frame(width: 200, height: 200)
        .padding()
}
```

## Aurora (`aurora`)

Soft, blurred colour blobs drift slowly behind your content.

- API: `AuroraBackground()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/AuroraBackground.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    AuroraBackground(colors: [.purple, .blue, .teal, .pink])
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    Text("Welcome").font(.largeTitle.bold())
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AuroraBackground view (iOS 17+). On a dark base color, draw one large circle per palette color (default purple, blue, teal, pink; 80% opacity, diameter 70% of the larger side). Each circle drifts on its own Lissajous path, x = cos(t·0.6 + phase)·30% width and y = sin(t·0.8 + phase·1.3)·30% height, where phase differs per index. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation) scaled by a speed parameter, blur the whole group with a ~60 pt radius, clip to bounds and hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Soft, slowly drifting colour blobs, heavily blurred. A calm animated
/// backdrop for onboarding screens, paywalls, or hero sections.
///
/// ```swift
/// ZStack {
///     AuroraBackground()
///         .ignoresSafeArea()
///     Text("Welcome").font(.largeTitle.bold())
/// }
/// ```
public struct AuroraBackground: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let speed: Double
    private let blurRadius: CGFloat
    private let baseColor: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    public init(
        colors: [Color] = [.purple, .blue, .teal, .pink],
        speed: Double = 0.4,
        blurRadius: CGFloat = 60,
        baseColor: Color = .black
    ) {
        self.colors = colors
        self.speed = speed
        self.blurRadius = blurRadius
        self.baseColor = baseColor
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: a still frame of the same blobs.
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                blobs(time: time, size: geometry.size)
            }
        }
        .background(baseColor)
        .clipped()
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func blobs(time: Double, size: CGSize) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(colors.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                blob(color: colors[index], index: index, time: time, size: size)
            }
        }
        .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
        .blur(radius: blurRadius)
    }

    private func blob(color: Color, index: Int, time: Double, size: CGSize) -> some View {
        let phase = Double(index) * 1.7
        let diameter = max(size.width, size.height) * 0.7
        let x = CGFloat(cos(time * 0.6 + phase)) * size.width * 0.3
        let y = CGFloat(sin(time * 0.8 + phase * 1.3)) * size.height * 0.3
        return Circle()
            .fill(color.opacity(0.8))
            .frame(width: diameter, height: diameter)
            .offset(x: x, y: y)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ZStack {
        AuroraBackground()
            .ignoresSafeArea()
        Text("Welcome")
            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
    }
}
```

## Rolling Number (`rolling-number`)

Digits roll like an odometer when the value changes.

- API: `RollingNumber(value:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/RollingNumber.swift

### Usage

```swift
RollingNumber(value: score)
    .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI RollingNumber view (iOS 17+) that displays a number with odometer-style digit rolling. Render Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit(), apply .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) so digits roll up when the value increases and down when it decreases, and animate changes with .snappy. Provide initialisers for Int and for Double with a FloatingPointFormatStyle.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A number whose digits roll up or down when the value changes, like an
/// odometer. Built on `contentTransition(.numericText)`.
///
/// ```swift
/// RollingNumber(value: score)
///     .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
/// ```
public struct RollingNumber: View {
    private let value: Double
    private let format: FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>
    private let animation: Animation

    public init(
        value: Double,
        format: FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double> = .number.precision(.fractionLength(0)),
        animation: Animation = .snappy
    ) {
        self.value = value
        self.format = format
        self.animation = animation
    }

    public init(value: Int, animation: Animation = .snappy) {
        self.init(value: Double(value), animation: animation)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(value, format: format)
            .monospacedDigit()
            .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
            .animation(animation, value: value)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var value = 1280
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                RollingNumber(value: value)
                    .font(.system(size: 56, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
                HStack {
                    Button("-") { value -= Int.random(in: 1...300) }
                    Button("+") { value += Int.random(in: 1...300) }
                }
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

## Particle Field (`particle-field`)

Drifting particles linked by faint lines, like a living constellation.

- API: `ParticleField()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/ParticleField.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()
    ParticleField(count: 60, color: .cyan)
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    Text("Connected").font(.largeTitle.bold())
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ParticleField view (iOS 17+) with count (50), color, speed (14 pt/s) and linkDistance (70 pt). Generate each particle's traits once from a seeded SplitMix64 generator: start position (0…1 in each axis), direction, speed factor (0.4–1.2), radius (1–2.8 pt) and opacity (0.4–1). In TimelineView(.animation) with a Canvas, compute each position as start + direction × time × speed × factor, wrapped around the canvas edges, so there is no stored state. Stroke a 0.8 pt line between every pair closer than linkDistance with opacity 0.35 × (1 − distance / linkDistance), then fill each particle as a circle. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Particles drifting slowly through the view, joined by faint lines when they
/// come close, like a constellation. A calm, techy background.
public struct ParticleField: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double
    private let linkDistance: CGFloat
    private let seeds: [ParticleSeed]

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of particles.
    ///   - color: Particle and line colour.
    ///   - speed: Drift speed in points per second.
    ///   - linkDistance: Particles closer than this are joined by a line (0 turns lines off).
    public init(count: Int = 50, color: Color = .white, speed: Double = 14, linkDistance: CGFloat = 70) {
        self.count = count
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
        self.linkDistance = linkDistance
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: 42)
        seeds = (0..<max(0, count)).map { _ in ParticleSeed(using: &generator) }
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let positions = seeds.map { $0.position(at: time, speed: speed, in: size) }
                if linkDistance > 0 {
                    for i in positions.indices {
                        for j in positions.indices where j > i {
                            let distance = hypot(positions[i].x - positions[j].x, positions[i].y - positions[j].y)
                            guard distance < linkDistance else { continue }
                            var line = Path()
                            line.move(to: positions[i])
                            line.addLine(to: positions[j])
                            context.stroke(line, with: .color(color.opacity(0.35 * (1 - distance / linkDistance))), lineWidth: 0.8)
                        }
                    }
                }
                for (seed, point) in zip(seeds, positions) {
                    let r = seed.radius
                    context.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: point.x - r, y: point.y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)),
                        with: .color(color.opacity(seed.opacity))
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

/// Fixed random traits of one particle. Its position is a pure function of
/// time, so the field needs no state and never drifts out of the view.
struct ParticleSeed {
    var start: CGPoint      // 0…1 in both axes
    var direction: Double   // radians
    var speedFactor: Double
    var radius: CGFloat
    var opacity: Double

    init(using generator: inout SplitMix64) {
        start = CGPoint(x: generator.unit(), y: generator.unit())
        direction = generator.unit() * 2 * .pi
        speedFactor = 0.4 + generator.unit() * 0.8
        radius = 1 + generator.unit() * 1.8
        opacity = 0.4 + generator.unit() * 0.6
    }

    func position(at time: Double, speed: Double, in size: CGSize) -> CGPoint {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return .zero }
        let travel = time * speed * speedFactor
        let x = (start.x * size.width + CGFloat(cos(direction) * travel)).wrapped(to: size.width)
        let y = (start.y * size.height + CGFloat(sin(direction) * travel)).wrapped(to: size.height)
        return CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
    }
}

/// Small deterministic random generator, so particle layouts are stable
/// between launches and previews.
struct SplitMix64: RandomNumberGenerator {
    private var state: UInt64

    init(seed: UInt64) { state = seed }

    mutating func next() -> UInt64 {
        state &+= 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15
        var z = state
        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) &* 0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9
        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) &* 0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB
        return z ^ (z >> 31)
    }

    /// A Double in 0..<1.
    mutating func unit() -> Double { Double.random(in: 0..<1, using: &self) }
}

extension CGFloat {
    /// Wraps the value into 0..<length.
    func wrapped(to length: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let r = truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: length)
        return r < 0 ? r + length : r
    }
}

#Preview {
    ParticleField()
        .background(Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.07, blue: 0.15))
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}
```

## Starfield (`starfield`)

Stars stream out of the centre and stretch into streaks: warp speed.

- API: `Starfield()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Starfield.swift

### Usage

```swift
Starfield()
    .background(.black)
    .ignoresSafeArea()

Starfield(count: 300, speed: 1.5) // warp jump
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Starfield view (iOS 17+) with count (200), speed (0.35 depth units per second) and color. Give each star a seeded random x and y in −1…1 and a depth in 0…1. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), compute z = 0.05 + 0.95 × fract(depth − time × speed), so stars approach the camera and wrap back to the far plane. Project with perspective: point = centre + (x, y) / z × 0.15 × half the larger side. Draw each star as a round-capped streak from its projection at a slightly larger z (z + min(0.08, speed × 0.05)) to its current projection, with opacity and line width growing as it gets closer. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Flying through space: stars stream out from the centre and stretch into
/// streaks as they pass the camera. Raise `speed` for a warp jump.
public struct Starfield: View {
    private let speed: Double
    private let color: Color
    private let stars: [Star]

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of stars.
    ///   - speed: Depth units per second; 0.3 cruises, 1.5 is warp speed.
    ///   - color: Star colour.
    public init(count: Int = 200, speed: Double = 0.35, color: Color = .white) {
        self.speed = speed
        self.color = color
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: 7)
        stars = (0..<max(0, count)).map { _ in
            Star(
                x: generator.unit() * 2 - 1,
                y: generator.unit() * 2 - 1,
                depth: generator.unit()
            )
        }
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let centre = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let scale = max(size.width, size.height) * 0.5
                // Streak length: where the star was a moment ago.
                let trail = min(0.08, speed * 0.05)
                for star in stars {
                    // Depth runs 1 (far) → 0.05 (at the camera), then wraps.
                    let z = 0.05 + 0.95 * (star.depth - time * speed).wrappedUnit
                    let zBehind = min(1, z + trail)
                    let head = CGPoint(x: centre.x + star.x / z * scale * 0.15, y: centre.y + star.y / z * scale * 0.15)
                    let tail = CGPoint(x: centre.x + star.x / zBehind * scale * 0.15, y: centre.y + star.y / zBehind * scale * 0.15)
                    let brightness = min(1, (1 - z) * 1.4)
                    var streak = Path()
                    streak.move(to: tail)
                    streak.addLine(to: head)
                    context.stroke(
                        streak,
                        with: .color(color.opacity(brightness)),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: max(0.6, (1 - z) * 2.4), lineCap: .round)
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private struct Star {
        var x: Double
        var y: Double
        var depth: Double
    }
}

private extension Double {
    /// Wraps the value into 0..<1.
    var wrappedUnit: Double {
        let r = truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
        return r < 0 ? r + 1 : r
    }
}

#Preview {
    Starfield()
        .background(.black)
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}
```

## Cover Flow (`cover-flow`)

Side items turn away in 3D, shrink and dim; the centre faces you.

- API: `CoverFlow(items) { item in }`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/CoverFlow.swift

### Usage

```swift
CoverFlow(albums) { album in
    Image(album.artwork)
        .resizable()
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
}
.frame(height: 220)
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI CoverFlow carousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding, itemWidth (140), spacing (−10) and maxAngle (50°). Use a horizontal ScrollView + LazyHStack with .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center) and contentMargins that centre the first and last items. In .visualEffect, read the item's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space, compute p = clamp((midX − viewport centre) / itemWidth, −1, 1) and apply rotation3DEffect of −p × maxAngle around the y axis (perspective 0.6), scale 1 − |p| × 0.18 and brightness −|p| × 0.25. Raise the selected item's zIndex. With Reduce Motion on, drop the rotation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A horizontal carousel in the style of Cover Flow: the centred item faces
/// you, and items to either side turn away in 3D, recede and dim. Items snap
/// to the centre.
public struct CoverFlow<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>?
    private let itemWidth: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let maxAngle: Double
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var internalSelection: Data.Element.ID?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: One item per element.
    ///   - selection: Optional binding to the centred item; set it to scroll.
    ///   - itemWidth: Width of each item in points.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between items (negative values overlap them).
    ///   - maxAngle: How far side items turn, in degrees.
    ///   - content: Builds one item, usually artwork.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>? = nil,
        itemWidth: CGFloat = 140,
        spacing: CGFloat = -10,
        maxAngle: Double = 50,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.selection = selection
        self.itemWidth = itemWidth
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.maxAngle = maxAngle
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            // Plain values for the visualEffect closure, which can't touch the view.
            let fallbackWidth = geometry.size.width
            let itemWidth = itemWidth
            let maxAngle = reduceMotion ? 0 : maxAngle
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        content(item)
                            .frame(width: itemWidth)
                            .visualEffect { view, proxy in
                                // -1 (one item left of centre) … 0 (centred) … 1.
                                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))
                                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))?.width ?? fallbackWidth
                                let clamped = max(-1, min(1, (frame.midX - viewport / 2) / itemWidth))
                                let angle = -clamped * maxAngle
                                return view
                                    .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(angle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
                                    .scaleEffect(1 - abs(clamped) * 0.18)
                                    .brightness(-abs(clamped) * 0.25)
                            }
                            // Centred item draws on top of its neighbours.
                            .zIndex(isSelected(item) ? 1 : 0)
                            .id(item.id)
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
                .frame(height: geometry.size.height)
            }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, max(0, (geometry.size.width - itemWidth) / 2), for: .scrollContent)
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .scrollPosition(id: selection ?? $internalSelection, anchor: .center)
        }
    }

    private func isSelected(_ item: Data.Element) -> Bool {
        (selection?.wrappedValue ?? internalSelection) == item.id
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Album: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let albums = [Color.red, .orange, .yellow, .green, .teal, .blue, .indigo, .purple]
        .enumerated().map { Album(id: $0, color: $1) }
    return CoverFlow(albums) { album in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
            .fill(album.color.gradient)
            .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
            .overlay(Image(systemName: "music.note").font(.largeTitle).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .frame(height: 200)
}
```

---

## Float 3D (`float-3d`)

The view hovers: a gentle bob, a slow 3D sway and a breathing shadow.

- API: `.float3D()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Float3D.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image("product")
    .resizable()
    .scaledToFit()
    .frame(width: 180)
    .float3D()

BadgeView()
    .float3D(height: 6, angle: 8, period: 4, shadow: false)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .float3D(height:angle:period:shadow:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), let t = time × 2π / period (3 s) and lift = 0.5 + 0.5·sin t. Rotate the content in 3D by sin(t/2) × angle (12°) around the y axis and cos(0.7t) × angle/2 around the x axis (perspective 0.5), and move it up by height (10 pt) × lift. Behind it, at the bottom, draw a black ellipse 12 pt tall, 18 pt below, that gets lighter (opacity 0.25 − 0.1·lift), narrower (scale x 0.75 − 0.15·lift) and blurrier (6 + 4·lift) as the view rises. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Makes a view hover in space: it bobs up and down and slowly sways in 3D,
/// while its shadow shrinks and grows underneath. For hero images, product
/// shots, badges and empty-state illustrations.
struct Float3DModifier: ViewModifier {
    var height: CGFloat
    var angle: Double
    var period: Double
    var shadow: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let t = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 2 * .pi / period
            // Bob: 0 at rest height, 1 at the top.
            let lift = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t)
            content
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(sin(t * 0.5) * angle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.5)
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(cos(t * 0.7) * angle * 0.5), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.5)
                .offset(y: -height * lift)
                .background(alignment: .bottom) {
                    if shadow {
                        Ellipse()
                            .fill(.black.opacity(0.25 - 0.1 * lift))
                            .frame(height: 12)
                            .scaleEffect(x: 0.75 - 0.15 * lift, y: 1)
                            .blur(radius: 6 + 4 * lift)
                            .offset(y: 18)
                    }
                }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Floats the view in 3D: a gentle bob, a slow sway and a breathing shadow.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("product")
    ///     .resizable()
    ///     .scaledToFit()
    ///     .frame(width: 180)
    ///     .float3D()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - height: How high the view rises, in points.
    ///   - angle: Maximum sway angle, in degrees.
    ///   - period: Seconds for one bob up and down.
    ///   - shadow: Draws a soft ground shadow under the view.
    func float3D(height: CGFloat = 10, angle: Double = 12, period: Double = 3, shadow: Bool = true) -> some View {
        modifier(Float3DModifier(height: height, angle: angle, period: period, shadow: shadow))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24, style: .continuous)
        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
        .frame(width: 140, height: 140)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "cube.fill").font(.system(size: 56)).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .float3D()
        .padding(60)
}
```
